product: commentary — no product (competitor teardown of Ryze Superfoods)
hook: "Ryze Superfoods is doing multiple 9 figs with 1 product and crazy creative strategy."
body: A full-funnel teardown of Ryze Superfoods: 5,324 active ads collapsing to just 6 headlines and 2 body copies — a pure creative-testing engine with locked copy. Format mix: 39% product-shot statics, 24% UGC talking head, 17% AI-animated 3D/Pixar storytelling, plus lifestyle/text-on-screen/meme/demo. 65% female-fronted; ~38% of avatar ads are synthetic 3D humans. TOF/MOF/BOF evenly split; BOF is graphic tiles (Labor Day bundles, "$27 from $45", "$0.90/cup"). Gaps: zero founder content, no podcast/interview, no before/after, no iPhone-notes.
idea: Massive creative × tiny copy: lock 2 body copies and iterate thousands of visual variants — the creative does the stopping, the copy does the qualifying.
sequencing: Scale proof: 5,324 ads, multiple 9 figs, 1 product.
The insight: 5,324 ads = 6 headlines × 2 body copies.
Format mix: statics 39%, UGC 24%, AI-animated 3D 17%.
Avatar mix: 65% female-fronted, 38% synthetic.
Funnel mix: TOF/MOF/BOF thirds; BOF = graphic tiles.
Copy angles: the two locked bodies + hook-angle variety.
8 takeaways (creative engine, AI animation edge, single-mechanic angles, advertorial-first LPs, demo testing via animation).
Gaps left on the table.
formatting: Very long data post: format mix, avatar mix, funnel mix, copy angles, lander destinations, 8 takeaways, gaps. One 38s video.
why_it_works: The collapse (5,324 → 6 headlines) is a stunning compression that reframes creative strategy from "write more" to "vary more," which is the actionable insight.
what_to_steal: The "2 body copies × thousands of creatives" operating model for LC: lock the waterproof/tarnish-proof copy, then generate endless visual variants — and the gap analysis (no founder, no podcast, no before/after) as LC's whitespace checklist.

body: Part 8 of a "passing on my best wisdom" countdown series (leading to the author deleting his profile): 21 years of hook-writing advice in under 600 words. Core law: "When you increase relevance, you increase conversion." The template: Location + Gender + Mechanism + Objection-killer + Deep pain ("Tennessee Woman Discovers Superfood That Melts Stubborn 'Flappy' Arm Fat"), with away-from-pain vs towards-pleasure variants, plus an instruction to train an AI hook-writer skill on the post.
cta: Follow @IMJustinBrooke so you don't miss the series.
idea: Relevance is the conversion lever: a 5-slot hook template (location, gender, mechanism, objection killer, deep pain) manufactures it on demand.
sequencing: Frame: wisdom series, pt 8, profile deletion countdown.
The law: relevance ↑ = conversion ↑.
Demo ladder: "Lose weight" → "Lose 30lbs" → "Lose 30lbs this summer."
Persona variants: hot-girl body vs flappy arms.
Geo variant: Tennessee woman + superfood.
Template decode: the 5 slots.
Pain vs pleasure markets.
The AI skill instruction: train your AI on this post.
formatting: Long text-lesson post with worked examples and a template breakdown. Thread-style.
why_it_works: The worked examples let the reader watch the template think, and the profile-deletion countdown manufactures scarcity around free wisdom.
what_to_steal: The 5-slot hook template for LC's ad headlines (location + persona + mechanism + objection killer + deep pain → e.g., "Texas mom discovers the waterproof stack that survives pool, sweat, and toddlers") and the countdown-to-deletion urgency frame for a content series.

product: Resilia aged garlic softgels ("Rosilia" in transcript)
hook: "Hi, how old is your grandson? … That's my grandson's grandson. … 102 years old."
body: A teardown of Resilia's AI street-interview ads starring 90+ year olds — "weirdly believable conversations" with "almost zero ad feeling," except none of it is real; the people are AI. The full transcript (video.twimg.com, 140s) is the ad itself: a 102-year-old interviewed on the street — "I am 102 years old and I live without doctors because of these three foods." The three: olive oil + turmeric rubbed into joints; raw onion with every meal ("the old Jews didn't have fancy medicines"); and aged garlic — "fermented in darkness for 20 months," creating S-Allyl Cysteine, triggering nitric oxide that "relaxes the blood vessels and helps dissolve the buildup clogging your arteries." The gate: "most aged garlic on the market is fake… The only one I trust is called Rosilia. Aged the full clinical dose… Two soft gels every morning." Closes: "They have a limited sale running right now."
cta: "I left the link below" + "limited sale running right now."
idea: Age-based authority marketing without the talent: AI-generated 102-year-olds deliver folk-wisdom countdowns that feel like documentaries, not ads.
sequencing: Street hook: the age reveal ("That's my grandson's grandson").
Authority frame: 102, no doctors, three foods; "save this video."
Foods 1-2: olive oil + turmeric for joints; raw onion for blood flow — with pill/blood-thinner objection kills.
The gap: onion doesn't clear calcium/cholesterol already stuck.
Food 3: aged garlic — 20-month ferment, nitric oxide, dissolves buildup.
Lineage proof: grandfather 96, father 89, no heart attacks.
The gate: most aged garlic is fake; only "Rosilia," two soft gels daily.
CTA: link below, limited sale; blessing close.
formatting: 140s vertical AI street interview (video.twimg.com): handheld realism, timestamped dialogue, rapid cuts between interviewer and the 102-year-old. Transcript in file.
why_it_works: Extreme age is unarguable authority — a 102-year-old doesn't need credentials — and the countdown format turns a pitch into advice, which is why it registers as "almost zero ad feeling."
what_to_steal: The entire interview-countdown architecture for LC: an AI elder (or real grandmother) counting down "3 jewelry rules" — the folk-wisdom listicle, the objection kills, the lineage proof, the single-product gate, the blessing close. LC's gate: "most 'waterproof' jewelry is flash-plated; only 14K PVD over steel passes."
